chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:
I was sitting in his presence when a man said to him: “Tell me about the wilayah of ʿAlī—was it from Allah or from His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?”

He became angry, then said: “Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم feared Allah too greatly to say what Allah had not commanded him with. Rather, He made it obligatory, just as Allah made obligatory the salat (prayer), zakat (alms-tax), sawm (fasting), and hajj (pilgrimage).”

key_terms.افْتَرَضَهُ: made it obligatory as a binding religious duty
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), one of the core obligatory acts
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.عَلِيٍّ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the subject of the wilayah mentioned

ai.seo_question: Is the wilayah of ʿAlī عليه السلام from Allah or from the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the wilayah of ʿAlī عليه السلام is not a personal declaration of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, but a divine obligation instituted by Allah. It places wilayah alongside foundational obligations such as salat, zakat, sawm, and hajj, highlighting its central place in faith and religious authority.
